finding.text: `Server/ServexFence.mjs` and the new `FENCE_SERVEX=1` switch in `Server/Browser.mjs:66` are not indexed in `Server/readme.md` or `Server/doc/browser.md`. `browser.md` is the doc for "the one Chromium launcher", and it now has an env switch it doesn't mention. Add one line to each, linking `Servex/doc/restart.md#when-servex-crashes…`.

Two Dictate scripts still call `route.continue()`, against the new "fallback, never continue" rule (`Servex/doc/restart.md:68`, `core/Test/doc/health.md:38`): `ux/Dictate/test/stall.mjs:53` and `refresh.mjs:138`. Both are for Whisper `:8178/inference`, not Servex, so they are safe today. Still, `ext/Refine/test/composer-flow.mjs:20` continues `**/api/refine**`; check that it never reaches `:8090`.

The shutdown snapshot overwrites a `sustain --restart` snapshot whenever the exit handler runs (`Servex/Servex.js:1587`). The revived agent would then lose its "(asked by X)" note, because `Agents.js:513` drops `by` once `how` is set. That's harmless today, since `sustain.mjs` kills with `taskkill /f` and no handler runs. It's worth a line in restart.md.

`process.on("unhandledRejection")` (`Servex/Servex.js:1603`) changes Node's default from "crash" to "log and continue" for all of Servex. That's a reasonable call and it's documented. Watch `servex.jsonl` for `unhandled_rejection` events piling up silently.

The new tests (`crash-revive.test.mjs`, `voice-page-refused.test.mjs`, `ServexFence.test.mjs`) run by hand only, like `revive-sweep.test.mjs`. No gate runs them. I ran all three in the worktree: 9, 3 and 7 checks passed.

If Servex crashes again during the stagger, every agent still waiting in the queue is lost. For each queued agent, the registry row keeps the boot id of the dying Servex until `reopen()` runs. The next boot only revives rows where `row.boot === prev.boot` (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:475`), so it buries those agents as "not open in the previous boot". With 17 agents and a 3 s gap, the queue takes 48 s to drain. The 09:47 crash came 62 s after a boot, which is exactly the case this change exists for. Fix: before queueing (`Agents.js:526`, `:536`), stamp each queued row with `this.boot`, or include the queued ids in a snapshot, and add a check 5 to `crash-revive.test.mjs` that boots twice in a row.

The task folder doesn't record this work, so a fresh agent couldn't continue from it. `session.jsonl` ends with the landing of `ac587d301` (09:09Z), and nothing in `session.jsonl` or `inbox.jsonl` mentions the stagger. The commits `02fe5aaaa` and `c6ee98e6b` sit unmerged on `worktree/servex-revive-stagger`. Add a log line, or a child task, that names the branch, the ask behind it and its merge state.

The "Crash and revive" section of `Servex/readme.md` (line 54) doesn't mention the stagger or `SERVEX_REVIVE_GAP_S`; only `doc/restart.md:65` does. Add half a sentence plus the link, so someone searching the env var finds it from the readme.

The `revive` line in `servex.jsonl` (`Agents.js:550`) lists every queued agent under `revived` and `told` before any of them has been reopened. A failure shows up later as a separate `revive-failed` line. `restart.md:65` says this, but anything that counts revives from the `revive` line will overcount.
I checked the race where a message arrives during the gap: `send()` → `wake()` reopens the agent, and the later `start()` finds it live and only tells it (`Agents.js:517-518`). That one is handled.
Tests in the stagger worktree: `node Servex/agents/crash-revive.test.mjs` passes 15 checks and `revive-sweep.test.mjs` passes 4. Neither runs in a gate.

The task folder still does not record the stagger work, as the last review's finding 2 said: `session.jsonl` has no line naming `worktree/servex-revive-stagger` (head `04581354c`, unmerged), the ask behind it or its merge state, so a fresh agent could not continue from this folder. Add one log line (or a child task) with the branch, the reason (the 09:47 crash 62 s after a 6-agent revive) and "awaiting merge".

An agent the owner stops while it waits in the revive queue comes back anyway: `stop()` on a row that is not live only marks it `stopped` (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:882-884`), but the queued `go()` calls `start()`, which reopens from the `row` it captured at boot (`Agents.js:519`) and never re-reads it, and `snapshot()` keeps listing it from `this.reviving` (`Agents.js:570`). Fix: in `go()`, skip the agent when its row now has `stopped_by` (or have `stop()` delete it from `this.reviving`), and add a check to `crash-revive.test.mjs`.

The last review's finding 1 is fixed: queued rows are re-stamped with the live boot before the queue starts (`Agents.js:537-541`), `snapshot()` lists the queue, and check 5 in `crash-revive.test.mjs` boots twice and gets all three back. In the worktree, `crash-revive.test.mjs` passes 20 checks and `revive-sweep.test.mjs` passes 4.
The last review's finding 3 is fixed: `Servex/readme.md:56` now names `SERVEX_REVIVE_GAP_S`, its default and the mid-turn-first order.

Requirements: ask 1 (revive after a crash with no snapshot) was already landed and is still covered by checks 1-3. This diff adds a mitigation for ask 2 (the stagger), and `Servex/doc/restart.md:63-65` says plainly that it is not a proven fix and how to judge it. That matches "otherwise, write down what to watch".

The `revive` line in `servex.jsonl` still counts queued agents as `revived` before they start (`Agents.js:557`). `restart.md:65` says so; a `queued` list beside `revived` would make the line honest without needing the doc.
Neither test runs in a gate. They only run when someone runs them by hand.

`Servex/doc/restart.md:71` still says `crash-revive.test.mjs` has "9 checks". It now prints "23 checks passed", and line 65 of the same file points at the same test, so the two lines disagree. Change 9 to 23, or drop the count.

Both findings from the last review are fixed. An agent stopped while it waits its turn stays stopped: `start()` re-reads the row's `stopped_by` (`Agents.js:519`), and `snapshot()` leaves it out (`Agents.js:571`). Check 6 covers it. Queued agents also survive a second crash (check 5).

Ran in the worktree (`worktree/servex-revive-stagger`, head ac6970093): `crash-revive.test.mjs` printed "23 checks passed" and `revive-sweep.test.mjs` printed "4 checks passed". No gate runs either test.

While an agent waits in the queue, its registry row reads `idle` or `working` (re-stamped at `Agents.js:537-541`), but no process is running. With the default gap of 3 s and 17 agents, the last one starts about 48 s after boot. `list_agents` and the dashboard show those agents as alive during that time. `restart.md:65` covers the `revive` line but not this.

The `revive` line in `servex.jsonl` counts queued agents as `revived` before they start. `restart.md:65` says so. A `queued` list next to `revived` would make the line accurate without needing the doc.

Requirements: asks 1, 3 and 4 landed in the earlier diff. This diff adds a mitigation for ask 2 (the stagger). `restart.md:63-65` says plainly that it is not a proven fix and explains how to judge it (if crashes soon after a revive boot keep their rate, set the gap to 0). That matches "otherwise, write down what to watch". The stagger lives in `revive()` alone, and the log names the alternative it rejected (staggering at `Servex.admission`). It is the simplest place for it.

A fresh agent could continue from this folder: `session.jsonl`'s last line names the branch, the head commit, the check command and the pending merge. The task has not landed yet. It has no landing line, and the branch is not merged into michael/dev.
